summary: Acknowledgement token drift during client-side backoff + connection migration causing duplicate external actions
description: Issue summary: The customer reports duplicate invocations of an external webhook (their downstream job queue) when a long-running tool execution is retried after a client-side backoff and the client moves to a new TCP/HTTP2 connection (connection migration). Impact: Duplicate side effects (duplicate downstream jobs) observed in production intermittently for a subset (~2%) of requests that hit long-running function calls. Scope: Customer uses Dedicated pool, runs high-concurrency multiplexed streams from the TypeScript SDK behind an edge proxy that performs connection pooling and occasional mid-session connection handover.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer sends multiplexed streaming request via TS SDK v1.14 with a tool invocation that triggers a webhook to their job queue (external HTTP POST).
Introduce simulated latency on the webhook (5+ seconds) to force the client SDK to hit internal retry/backoff logic while still holding the stream open.
Simulate client connection migration by closing the HTTP/2 stream mid-backoff and allowing the client to re-establish a new stream within the same logical session.
Observe duplicate webhook posts in customer job queue logs for ~1-3% of runs under these conditions.
logs: Customer webhook logs show two POSTs with same payload spaced ~6s apart: 2026-02-28T18:14:22Z and 2026-02-28T18:14:28Z

Redwood request traces (trace-id: rbw-7b-20260228-xx) show original stream session with ack nonce 'n=v4-9f3a' and resumed stream reporting ack nonce 'n=v4-9f3a�' (trailing null), likely normalization issue in proxy
Edge proxy (provider X) logs: header rewrite on connection handover, truncated idempotency token to first 16 chars in some frames
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: idempotency/confirmation token normalization mismatch between original stream and resumed stream after connection migration; downstream confirmation check failed leading to a second execution.

Reproduced locally with TS SDK + mocked edge proxy that rewrites headers on connection migration. When the token is truncated or has a non-printable suffix, server-side idempotency map treats resumed acknowledgement as distinct, so tool run is re-issued.
Python SDK does not show same behaviour in customer tests because their Python clients use single-request blocking pattern (no multiplex) and do not trigger connection migration in same way.

Observed additional factor: some proxies insert zero bytes (�) or split long header values across pseudo-frames; our header canonicalization path currently trims trailing control chars but only on initial request path, not on resumed connection path.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Kumar (Support): Acknowledged issue and requested customer debug logs and example trace. Asked for SDK versions and edge proxy vendor. (waiting on customer)

2026-03-02 - Customer (DataBright SRE - Priya Menon): Provided traces, SDK versions: ts-sdk@1.14.0, py-sdk@1.12.2, proxy: EdgeX v3.2. Customer confirms duplicates are ~2% and correlated with proxy handovers.
2026-03-03 - Miguel Torres (Infra Eng): Reproduced locally with our proxy shim. Created PR to add normalization on resume path. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2487

2026-03-04 - SRE (Liam O'Neill): Added temporary mitigation in dedicated fleet: enable strict header passthrough on customer edge route to avoid proxy truncation. Monitoring for duplicate webhook counts.
analysis: Root cause: token normalization inconsistency between initial connection handling and stream-resume code path. When an idempotency/confirmation token is mutated (truncated, padded with control characters, or split), the resumed session supplies a different canonical token and server treats resumed invocation as a new request.
Contributing factors: multiplexed TS SDK using connection migration semantics, certain edge proxies that rewrite or split headers, and lack of resume-path normalization in the serving runtime.
resolution: Hotfix rollout: Applied runtime change to canonicalize idempotency tokens on resume and initial request paths. Deployed to Dedicated customer pool in us-east 2026-03-05 03:00 UTC.

Customer mitigation: Advised DataBright to enable 'preserve-headers' mode on their EdgeX routes and increase webhook idempotency resilience (idempotency key in payload as fallback) until hotfix rollout is verified.
Post-deploy monitoring: Duplicate webhook rate dropped from ~2% to <0.02% in 48h window; no new regressions observed.

Follow-up actions: Add unit tests for header-splitting/resume path normalization, update SDK docs with guidance on best-effort idempotency keys in payload for proxy-prone networks, track a follow-up internal task INT-3410 for improved diagnostics on header anomalies.
